clue.text: It offers no help to the single minded

definitions.text: It offers no help to the single minded

parts.words: It offers no help to the single minded
parts.note: read 'single minded' as people who mean to stay unmarried: a matchmaking agency is the one place they would never go for help

explanation.surface: A grumble that nothing out there helps people who focus on one thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A matchmaking agency exists to pair off unattached people, so anyone determined to stay unattached gets nothing from it.

clue.text: Bowls as played in the 18th century

definitions.text: Bowls as played in the 18th century

parts.words: Bowls as played in the 18th century
parts.note: not the lawn game: bowls here are drinking vessels, which were played by rubbing their wet rims in Georgian times

explanation.surface: A history note on how the lawn game was played two centuries ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowls (the lawn game, popular in Britain) is the false trail; the bowls are tuned glass vessels, an instrument Benjamin Franklin refined in the 1760s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuned drinking vessels rubbed with a moist finger were a fashionable instrument in Georgian drawing rooms.

clue.text: Criticism making theatre company take cover

parts.note: REP is short for repertory, a theatre company performing a season of plays
a roof is the cover over a building

explanation.surface: Actors running for shelter after a bad review.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebuke or telling-off is a form of criticism.

clue.text: The key from one's time as tenant

parts.note: one is I, so one's (one has) gives I plus S
a let is a period of renting a property

explanation.surface: Someone recalls the door key from their days of renting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key' is not a door key but a low island, as in the Florida Keys.
explanation.definitionFit: A key (or cay) is a small low island, the same thing as a tiny isle.

clue.text: Punishing run accepted as challenge

definitions.meaning: a punishment in which the offender ran between two lines of men striking him
throwing down a glove was the old way of issuing a challenge to fight

explanation.surface: A gruelling run taken on as a dare.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from old customs: the double file of beaters, and the knight's thrown-down glove.

clue.text: Barley brew making one indistinct

indicators.note: to brew is to mix and stew ingredients together, so the letters of the grain are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Drinking barley beer leaves someone hazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes or images that are blurred and unclear are described this way.

clue.text: Change plan to introduce new standard on board

indicators.note: introduce means bring something inside, so the letter for new is put into the reworked plan

parts.note: to change a plan is to redesign it

explanation.surface: A committee decides to alter the scheme and bring in a fresh benchmark on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' is a flag and 'on board' means aboard ship; the board is not a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: This red flag is flown by British merchant ships, a standard carried aboard.

clue.text: On the rocks coming out of the Silver Ring

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a ring is a round shape

explanation.surface: A punter goes broke leaving the cheap enclosure at the racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Silver Ring is a cheaper betting enclosure at British racecourses, and 'on the rocks' suggests being broke; here it is a stranded ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship stuck on the rocks has run onto the seabed or shore, i.e. it is stranded.

clue.text: Sea dog's craft

parts.note: not an old sailor's skill: read it as the vessel of a dog of the sea, a fast racing hound on the waves

explanation.surface: The seamanship of a veteran sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast transatlantic liners of the late Victorian era were nicknamed after the racing dog for their speed.

clue.text: Stupid rule set up, putting somebody in grave situation

indicators.note: something stupid is muddled and senseless, so the following letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foolish regulation is introduced that leaves someone in a serious fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid' looks like it describes the rule, but it signals rearranging RULE SET UP; 'grave situation' sounds like a crisis but is literally a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means burial, the act of laying a body in a tomb.

clue.text: Rustic dialect

definitions.meaning: the plainest Greek architectural order was regarded as rustic and simple
The broad Scots dialect of north-east Scotland

explanation.definitionFit: The word is used for a plain, countrified style and for a broad rural speech of Scotland.

clue.text: Hit 150 before getting dismissed

indicators.note: before puts the number in front of the word for dismissed

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals
a batsman who is dismissed in cricket is out

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores 150 runs before being given out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a dismissed batsman is 'out', and 150 sounds like his score.
explanation.definitionFit: A clout is a heavy blow, so to clout is to strike hard.

clue.text: Dangerous creature producing natural disturbance among soldiers

indicators.note: among places the jumbled letters inside the soldiers' letters

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers

indicators.note: a disturbance stirs things up, so the letters of natural are put out of order

explanation.surface: A natural upheaval breaks out among the troops, creating a deadly beast.
explanation.definitionFit: This large hairy spider has a venomous bite and is feared as a dangerous animal.

clue.text: His son will never succeed

parts.note: succeed means inherit the title: a peerage held only for life cannot pass to an heir

explanation.surface: A father's gloomy prediction about his boy's prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: A British life peer sits in the House of Lords but the title dies with him, so his son cannot follow him into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A peerage granted for the holder's lifetime only is not hereditary, so no heir takes it on.

clue.text: One who can foretell result of mixing port with cider

indicators.note: mixing blends things together, so the letters of the two drinks are combined and rearranged

explanation.surface: A fortune teller who knows what happens when you blend port and cider.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forecasts the future makes predictions, the agent noun of predict.

clue.text: Mongrel's variegated fare rejected

parts.note: pied means patched with different colours

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for fare is read backwards

parts.note: to fare is to go, as in how did it go or fare

explanation.surface: A dog spurns its mixed food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like food but is the verb meaning get on; the definition carries the clue's 's (mongrel is).
explanation.definitionFit: A stray half-wild dog of Asian villages is a classic mongrel.

clue.text: In-joke about southern rustic

indicators.note: about means round, so the two pieces sit round the letter for southern

parts.note: being in means being at home
a pun is a joke on words

explanation.surface: A private joke about a Southerner who is a bit of a country bumpkin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In-joke' looks like one word but splits into 'In' (at home) and 'joke'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun cloth was made in the home, so the word came to mean plain and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Young chap holding Oxford degree is scooped up

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the degree sits inside the young man's word

parts.note: a lad is a young chap
PPE is Philosophy, Politics and Economics, a famous Oxford degree

explanation.surface: A young man with an Oxford degree is snapped up by an employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Scooped up suggests being hired eagerly; here it is a cat lapping up milk with its tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: To lap up a liquid is to take it in with the tongue, scooping it.

clue.text: Extremely powerful bishop taking pawn on row

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
taken as written
a tiff is a quarrel or row

explanation.surface: A chess bishop captures a pawn along a rank.
explanation.walkthrough: Pawn, bishop and row all suggest chess, but the bishop is the Pope, and row rhymes with cow (a quarrel).
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope, supreme bishop of Rome, is called the Supreme Pontiff.

clue.text: Coastal road in once rich resort

indicators.note: re-sort means sort again, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A clifftop road in a seaside town that was once wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town but is re-sort, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, as on the French Riviera.

clue.text: A help for climbers performing with muscular trouble

parts.note: a cramp is a painful muscle spasm
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: A mountaineer struggles on despite a cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiked metal frame fixed to boots gives grip on ice to mountaineers.

clue.text: Fashionable business failing

parts.note: something fashionable is in
a firm is a business

explanation.surface: A trendy company is going under.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weak from age or illness is failing in health.

clue.text: Judgment imprisoning individual produces feeling

indicators.note: imprisoning means locking up inside, so the letter for one sits within the court's word

parts.note: a court's judgment is a sentence
I is one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A court verdict jails a person and stirs emotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive.

clue.text: Famine, having run out, results in this

indicators.note: out means removed, so the run letter is taken away

parts.note: a dearth is a famine or scarcity
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A grim warning about what famine leads to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' is a link; the definition points back to famine, which ends in this outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Starvation in a famine ends lives, so its outcome is mortality.

clue.text: Simple garment, indeed, hot Indian needs

indicators.note: needs here reads as contains: the run of words has the garment within it

explanation.surface: In hot weather an Indian man wants simple clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The garment sits across 'inDEED HOT Indian'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by Hindu men, a simple wrapped garment.

clue.text: Not the way in which Society has divided to survive

indicators.note: the letter for Society splits the exit word in two

parts.note: the way that is not in is the way out

explanation.surface: A society has split over which way is not the entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to live on, to survive.

clue.text: I am ready to act with you, say, without rehearsing

parts.note: I am contracts to I'm
prompt means ready and quick to act

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be heard, giving a letter of the same sound

parts.note: the pronoun you is said exactly like the letter U

explanation.surface: An actor tells a partner they are ready to go on together without rehearsal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something impromptu is done on the spur of the moment, unprepared.

clue.text: Somehow I'd a note supervisors accepted with previous reference

indicators.note: accepted means taken in, so the jumbled letters take the supervisors inside
somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put into an unknown new order

parts.note: foremen are supervisors of workers

explanation.surface: Managers somehow accept a memo that refers back to an earlier one.
explanation.walkthrough: The supervisors are taken inside the scrambled letters, splitting them into A and TIONED; the definition means mentioned earlier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mentioned before in a text has been referred to previously.
